note: Lunch that travels, and dinner when nobody wants to cook. Every one of these has a specific structural idea in it — something that keeps the bread from going soggy, or gets the filling to hold together, or makes it good four hours later in a cooler.

recipes.title: Bánh Mì
recipes.blurb: Vietnam by way of the French colonial baguette: quick-pickled daikon and carrot, cold herbs, chile, and something savory in the middle. The pickle is the whole sandwich.
steps: Pickle first: dissolve the sugar and salt in the rice vinegar plus 1/3 cup warm water, pour it over the daikon and carrot, and leave 30 minutes. They will still be crunchy — that is the point. This is đồ chua and it keeps three weeks in the fridge.
Marinate the tofu slabs in the soy and hoisin for 10 minutes, then pan-fry in the oil over medium-high, 3 minutes a side, until lacquered.
Stir the sriracha into the mayonnaise.
Pull some of the soft interior out of the baguette so the sandwich closes. Toast the halves cut side down in a dry pan for a minute.
Build: spicy mayonnaise on both sides, tofu, a generous fistful of drained pickles, cucumber spears, whole cilantro sprigs, jalapeño. Press it closed and cut on a hard diagonal.

omnivore.label: Pork or pâté
omnivore.note: Thin-sliced grilled pork shoulder in the same marinade, or a smear of pâté under the mayonnaise, which is the traditional version.

recipes.kidTweak: Leave the jalapeño and sriracha off. Sweet pickled carrot and lacquered tofu in bread is not a hard sell.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Whole cilantro sprigs, stems and all. Chopped cilantro disappears; sprigs give you a mouthful of it, which is what the sandwich is for.
recipes.leftovers: The pickles keep 3 weeks and improve. Assemble sandwiches to order.
recipes.prepAhead: Pickle a big jar on Sunday and bánh mì becomes a ten-minute lunch all week.

recipes.title: Philly Mushroom Cheesesteak
recipes.blurb: Mushrooms and onions chopped on the griddle the way South Philly does it, piled into a roll with provolone melted over the top. The chopping is the technique.
steps: Get the skillet properly hot. Add the oil, then the mushrooms in one layer, and leave them alone 4 minutes so they brown instead of stew.
Add the onions and pepper and cook 6 minutes more.

Now chop: work two spatulas or a bench scraper through the pile on the heat, cutting everything smaller as it cooks. Ten passes. This is what a Philly griddle cook does to a steak and it is why the filling packs into a roll instead of sliding out.
Add the butter, soy sauce, salt and pepper. Cook 2 more minutes until nothing is watery. (A teaspoon of Worcestershire belongs here if nobody at the table is vegetarian — it contains anchovy.)
Divide the pile into four roll-shaped heaps in the pan, lay cheese over each, and cover the skillet for 60 seconds to melt.
Slide a split roll upside down over each heap, then scoop underneath with the spatula and flip the whole thing into the roll. That is the move.

omnivore.label: Shaved ribeye
omnivore.note: Half a pound of very thinly sliced steak, chopped on the griddle exactly the same way, added at the end so it cooks in 2 minutes.

recipes.kidTweak: Cut the sandwich in half crosswise. It is mushrooms, onions and melted cheese in bread — no negotiation needed.
recipes.restaurantTouch: The chop on the heat. It is one minute of work and it is what makes this taste like a cheesesteak rather than a mushroom sandwich.
recipes.leftovers: The filling keeps 3 days and is very good on eggs or pasta. Assemble to order.

recipes.title: Tempeh Reuben
recipes.blurb: Marinated tempeh, real sauerkraut, Swiss and a homemade Russian dressing, griddled in a rye sandwich until the cheese runs. The kraut gets squeezed — that is the trick.
steps: Steam the tempeh planks 10 minutes before anything else. Tempeh has a bitter edge raw and steaming takes it away — this is the step that decides whether people like tempeh.
Marinate them in the soy, vinegar, paprika, coriander and maple for 15 minutes, then fry in the oil until browned on both sides.
Russian dressing: mayonnaise, ketchup, horseradish and chopped pickle.
Squeeze the sauerkraut hard in your fist. Wet kraut makes a soggy reuben, every time.
Butter the outsides of the bread. Build inside: dressing, Swiss, tempeh, kraut, more Swiss, dressing. Cheese on both sides glues the sandwich together.
Griddle over medium, weighted with a heavy pan, 4 minutes a side, until the rye is dark and the cheese is running out the edges.

omnivore.label: Corned beef
omnivore.note: Warm sliced corned beef, piled higher than seems reasonable, in place of the tempeh.

recipes.kidTweak: Sauerkraut is a big flavor. Make theirs as a plain Swiss grilled cheese on the same griddle.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Cheese against both slices of bread, filling in the middle. It is structural, not indulgent.
recipes.leftovers: Assemble to order. Cooked tempeh keeps 4 days and is good chopped into salads.
recipes.heartNote: Sauerkraut and rye bread are both salty; at about 900 mg a sandwich this is a once-in-a-while lunch. Rinsing the kraut cuts roughly a third of that.
recipes.allergenNote: Contains soy, wheat, dairy and egg.

recipes.title: Smashed Chickpea Salad Sandwich
recipes.blurb: Ten minutes, no cooking, and it holds up in a lunchbox better than anything with meat in it. Celery and pickle do the work here.
steps: Smash the chickpeas with a fork or a potato masher until about two-thirds are broken and a third are still whole. That mix of textures is what makes it read as a salad rather than a paste.
Fold in everything else except the bread and the lettuce and tomato.
Taste for salt, lemon and pepper. It should be sharper than seems right in the bowl — bread mutes everything.
Build on toasted bread with lettuce laid against both slices as a moisture barrier, then tomato, then the filling.
recipes.kidTweak: Serve it as a dip with crackers and cucumber rounds instead of a sandwich. Same lunchbox, less negotiation.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Lettuce against the bread, not on top of the filling. It keeps a packed sandwich edible four hours later.
recipes.leftovers: The filling keeps 4 days. Do not build sandwiches ahead.
recipes.heartNote: About 13 g of protein and 11 g of fiber a sandwich, with a quarter of the saturated fat of the tuna-salad version.

recipes.title: Grilled Cheese and Real Tomato Soup
recipes.blurb: Mayonnaise on the outside of the bread instead of butter — it browns more evenly and cannot burn. The soup is four ingredients and forty minutes.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium for 10 minutes until soft and sweet. Add the garlic for 1.
Add the tomatoes, broth, sugar and salt. Simmer 25 minutes — long enough for the canned-tomato tinny edge to cook off completely.
Blend with the basil until smooth, then stir in the milk. Off the heat from here.
Grate both cheeses and mix them. Cheddar for flavor, gruyère for the melt; either alone is a compromise.
Spread mayonnaise on the outsides of the bread. It has a higher smoke point than butter and browns into an even, blistered crust.
Griddle over medium-low — low and slow, 4 minutes a side — so the cheese is fully molten by the time the bread is dark. Cut on the diagonal and serve with the soup for dipping.
recipes.kidTweak: This is the dinner children remember. Let them dip.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Medium-low heat, and a lid for the first two minutes. High heat gives you a browned sandwich full of solid cheese.
recipes.leftovers: The soup keeps 5 days and freezes 3 months. Sandwiches, obviously, do not.
recipes.heartNote: Bread and cheese are both salty before anything is added, which is why the soup takes half a teaspoon of salt rather than a full one and the sandwiches take five ounces of cheese for four rather than eight. It still eats like the diner version.

recipes.title: Croque Monsieur
recipes.blurb: A ham and cheese sandwich with béchamel inside and on top, run under the broiler until it blisters. France's answer to lunch, and the sauce takes six minutes.
steps: Béchamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook 2 minutes without letting it color. Add the milk in three additions, whisking smooth each time, and simmer 4 minutes until it coats a spoon.
Off the heat, add the nutmeg, salt, pepper and a third of the gruyère. Nutmeg in a béchamel is not optional in France.
Toast the bread lightly. Spread mustard on four slices, then a thin layer of béchamel, then ham and half the remaining cheese. Close the sandwiches.
Set them on a sheet pan. Spoon the rest of the béchamel over the tops and edges, and cover with the last of the cheese.
Broil 4-6 inches from the element for 4-5 minutes until bubbling and browned in spots. Watch it constantly.
Rest 2 minutes before eating. Molten béchamel is a genuine hazard.

vegetarianSwap.label: Croque aux champignons
vegetarianSwap.note: Mushrooms browned hard with thyme in place of the ham. With this much béchamel and gruyère nobody feels shortchanged.

recipes.kidTweak: Cut into fingers. It is essentially a very serious grilled cheese.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Add a fried egg on top and it becomes a croque madame, which is the better sandwich and nobody argues about it.
recipes.leftovers: Eat it hot. Béchamel keeps 3 days and makes an excellent base for a gratin.
recipes.heartNote: Rich by design — gruyère, butter and ham together put this among the highest saturated fat and sodium plates in the collection. It is a Sunday lunch with a salad, not a weekday habit.

recipes.title: Oyster Mushroom Po'Boy
recipes.blurb: Torn oyster mushrooms in a cornmeal crust taste uncannily like fried oysters. Dressed New Orleans style — lettuce, tomato, pickle and rémoulade.
steps: Soak the torn mushrooms in the buttermilk and hot sauce for 10 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal, flour, paprika, cayenne, garlic powder and salt. Dredge each piece, pressing the coating on, and let them sit 5 minutes so the crust sets.
Air fry at 400°F for 12-14 minutes, misting with oil and shaking halfway — or shallow-fry in the oil over medium-high, 3 minutes a side.
Rémoulade: mayonnaise, mustard, horseradish, lemon juice and a shake of hot sauce.
'Dressed' in New Orleans means lettuce, tomato, pickle and mayonnaise. Build that way, pile the mushrooms in hot, and eat immediately.

omnivore.label: Shrimp po'boy
omnivore.note: The same buttermilk soak, the same cornmeal dredge, 8 minutes at 400°F. It is the original for a reason.

recipes.kidTweak: Serve the crisp mushrooms as nuggets with the rémoulade for dipping and skip the cayenne.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Tear the mushrooms rather than cutting them. The ragged edges are what catch the crust and crisp.
recipes.leftovers: Eat immediately. The rémoulade keeps a week.

recipes.title: Bean and Avocado Torta
recipes.blurb: Mexico's great sandwich: a crusty roll, refried beans smeared on one side as glue, avocado, pickled onion and salsa. Fifteen minutes.
steps: Quick-pickle the onion: toss the slices with the juice of one lime and 1/4 teaspoon salt and leave them. Twenty minutes turns them pink and sweet.
Fry the garlic and cumin in the oil for 30 seconds, add the beans and 1/4 cup water, and mash them into a thick paste over medium heat, 5 minutes. Season with the rest of the salt.
Split the rolls and toast them cut side down in a dry pan.
Spread the warm beans thickly on the bottom half — they are the glue that keeps everything else in place.
Layer avocado, cheese, salsa, pickled onion, lettuce, cilantro and jalapeño. Press the sandwich down hard before cutting; a torta is supposed to be compressed.

omnivore.label: Milanesa
omnivore.note: A breaded, fried thin chicken cutlet laid over the beans is the classic torta de milanesa.

recipes.kidTweak: Beans, avocado and cheese only. The pickled onions are usually the sticking point.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Refried beans as the moisture barrier. It is why a torta survives a lunchbox and a sub does not.
recipes.leftovers: Beans keep 4 days; pickled onions keep 2 weeks and improve everything they touch.

recipes.title: Pressed Caprese Sandwich
recipes.blurb: Tomato, mozzarella, basil and good oil, pressed for an hour so the bread drinks the juices. Built for a cooler and better after two hours than at zero.
steps: Salt the tomato slices and lay them on a towel for 10 minutes. Blot them. Unsalted, undrained tomato is what destroys a packed sandwich.
Rub the cut faces of the bread with the halved garlic clove, then drizzle with half the oil and all the vinegar.
Layer mozzarella first against the bottom bread, then tomato, basil, arugula, roasted peppers, pepper and the rest of the oil.
Close it, wrap it tightly in parchment or foil, and put a heavy pan on top for at least an hour — up to four in the fridge.
Cut into four through the wrapping. The bread should be compressed and stained pink at the edges.

omnivore.label: Add salami or prosciutto
omnivore.note: A few thin slices against the top half, so the fat softens into the crumb while it presses.

recipes.kidTweak: Cheese-and-tomato bread that has been squashed on purpose. Skip the arugula and balsamic on theirs.
recipes.restaurantTouch: The press. An hour under a cast-iron pan turns four separate ingredients into one thing.
recipes.leftovers: Best 1-4 hours after pressing. Keeps overnight but the bread softens.

recipes.title: New England Crab Roll
recipes.blurb: Cold lump crab dressed barely at all, piled in a griddled buttered roll. Five ingredients, and the restraint is the recipe.
steps: Pick through the crab for shell. Fold — do not stir — the mayonnaise, lemon juice, celery, chives and Old Bay through it. Five or six strokes.
Taste before adding salt. Crab is naturally saline and Old Bay is mostly salt.
Butter the outsides of the rolls and griddle them on both flat sides over medium until golden. This is the New England move and it is worth the two minutes.
Line each roll with a lettuce leaf, pile the crab in high, and finish with more chives and a lemon wedge.

vegetarianSwap.label: Hearts of palm roll
vegetarianSwap.note: Shredded artichoke hearts, squeezed dry and dressed identically, in the same griddled roll.

recipes.kidTweak: Sweet crab in a buttery roll. Leave the Old Bay off theirs if they are cautious.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Three tablespoons of mayonnaise for a whole container of crab. Anything more and you are eating mayonnaise.
recipes.leftovers: Eat the day it is made.
recipes.heartNote: Crab is one of the leanest proteins in the store — about 30 g a roll with barely any fat beyond the dressing.
recipes.allergenNote: Contains shellfish, wheat, egg and dairy.

recipes.title: Everything-Bagel Egg Salad
recipes.blurb: Jammy eggs rather than hard, folded with yogurt and everything seasoning. Ten minutes for the best lunchbox sandwich there is.
steps: Lower the eggs into already-boiling water and cook exactly 9 minutes, then ice-bath them. Nine minutes gives a yolk that is set but still bright and slightly fudgy — hard-boiled eggs are what make egg salad chalky.
Peel and chop coarsely. Some big pieces, some small.
Fold in the yogurt, mayonnaise, mustard, everything seasoning, chives, celery, lemon and pepper.
Taste before salting — everything seasoning brings its own.
Build on toasted bread with lettuce against both slices.
recipes.kidTweak: Serve it on crackers or in a lettuce cup. Leave the everything seasoning off theirs and add a little more mustard.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Yogurt for most of the binder, mayonnaise for the rest. You get the richness without the sandwich turning into a paste.
recipes.leftovers: Keeps 3 days. Build sandwiches to order.
recipes.heartNote: Eight eggs across four sandwiches is two each — fine for most healthy adults. For someone managing existing heart disease, use four whole eggs and six whites.
recipes.allergenNote: Contains egg, wheat, dairy and sesame.

recipes.title: Vegetarian Italian Sub
recipes.blurb: Everything a real Italian sub does — oil and vinegar, oregano, sharp cheese, pickled heat — with roasted peppers, marinated artichokes and provolone carrying it.
steps: Whisk the oil, vinegar, oregano, pepper flakes and salt into a dressing. This is the thing that makes a sub taste like a sub, and it goes on last.
Split the rolls without cutting all the way through, so they hinge.
Layer cheese against the bottom, then artichokes, roasted peppers, olives, onion and tomato.
Pile the shredded lettuce on top and dress it directly, then close the roll and press. Dressing the lettuce rather than the bread keeps everything below it crisp.
Wrap tightly in parchment and give it 15 minutes before cutting.

omnivore.label: The full salumi
omnivore.note: Capicola, salami and provolone, layered in the same order under the vegetables.

recipes.kidTweak: Cheese, tomato and lettuce with a little oil. Skip the olives, onion and pepper flakes.
recipes.restaurantTouch: Dress the lettuce, not the bread. Every good sub shop does this and almost no home cook does.
recipes.leftovers: Wrapped tight, it holds 4 hours in a cooler and improves for the first two.
